st.headline: S&P 500 ends higher as strong inflation data cements rate hike bets
st.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.98 per cent to 52,573.29 points.
fullText: NEW YORK – Wall Street ended higher on Sept 11 as oil prices retreated and strong consumer price data reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week to fight inflation.

Dell, maker of artificial intelligence servers, soared 12 per cent to a record high. Hewlett Packard Enterprise jumped 12 per cent and HP gained 8.4 per cent after Oracle’s quarterly results topped estimates. Oracle dipped 1.8 per cent.
US consumer prices accelerated in August as the cost of petrol rebounded after two straight monthly declines, adding pressure on the Fed to tighten monetary policy to fight inflation.

Interest rate futures now reflect a nearly 90 per cent probability that the central bank will raise rates at its policy meeting on Sept 16, according to the CME FedWatch tool. This is up from a 72 per cent likelihood on Sept 10.
“That’s pretty much as close to a slam dunk as you’re going to get,” said Thomas Martin, senior ⁠portfolio manager at Globalt Investments in Atlanta.
“The Fed will do the right thing and raise rates, and that is good at the margin for keeping inflation in check.”
The S&P 500 climbed 0.86 per cent to end the session at 7,656.98 points.
The Nasdaq gained 0.96 per cent to 26,333.04 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.98 per cent to 52,573.29 points.
Nine of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes rose, led by communication services, up 1.35 per cent, followed by a 1.13 per cent gain in consumer discretionary.
Volume on US exchanges was relatively light, with 14 billion shares traded, compared with an average of 14.9 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions.
The CBOE Volatility Index, Wall Street’s fear gauge, fell two points to 15.88.

The Sept 11 rally follows recent nervousness on Wall Street related to inflation and rising long-term Treasury yields, as well as concerns about massive spending to build AI data centres. The S&P 500 is down about 2 per cent from its record-high close on Aug 13, and it remains up 12 per cent in 2026.
For the week, the S&P 500 dipped 0.8 per cent and the Nasdaq lost 0.7 per cent.

The S&P 500’s recent decline, coupled with a strong earnings outlook, has the benchmark trading at 19 times expected earnings. This is its cheapest since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariff announcements threw global markets into a tailspin.

Oil prices fell but remained up around 9 per cent for the week as attacks along Middle East shipping routes stoked concerns about prolonged supply disruptions. Brent crude futures slipped almost 3 per cent but were still above US$104 a barrel.
Shares of ACV Auctions soared 44 per cent after online vehicle auctioneer Copart agreed to buy it in a nearly US$1.9 billion (S$2.4 billion) deal.
Advancing issues outnumbered falling ones within the S&P 500 by a 2.1:1 ratio.
The S&P 500 posted eight new highs and nine new lows; the Nasdaq recorded 45 new highs and 182 new lows. REUTERS

cna.headline: Festival Of Thrills at RWS returns with Halloween Horror Nights, Minions live show, racing experiences and more
cna.teaser: Festival Of Thrills will run till Nov 1 at Resorts World Sentosa and comprises numerous activities and experiences.
fullText: Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) has brought back its Festival Of Thrills programme this month. Comprising numerous exhilarating experiences across the resort, Festival Of Thrills will run till Nov 1.
One of the programme's biggest highlights is, of course, the iconic Halloween Horror Nights, returning to Universal Studios Singapore for its 14th edition.

Happening on selected nights between 25 Sep and 1 Nov, this year's Halloween Horror Nights will feature haunted houses themed after the likes of a broadcasting station and a karang guni shop, as well as numerous horror-themed live shows.
Tickets for Halloween Horror Nights 2026 are currently on sale via Resorts World Sentosa's website and Klook , with regular ticket prices starting at S$68.

View this post on Instagram Beyond Halloween Horror Nights, Universal Studios Singapore will also host Trick Or Thrills for family-friendly fun. Visitors can look forward to a Halloween-themed live show starring the Minions and meet-and-greet sessions with popular characters like Kuromi, Cookie Monster and Shrek.
Trick Or Thrills is included with regular admission to Universal Studios Singapore.

Over at Singapore Oceanarium, visitors can enjoy the neon-inspired Into The Glowcean experience, featuring engaging activities and installations such as light painting, glowing marine-life sculptures, and a silent disco.
Into The Glowcean runs until Nov 1, with some activities taking place only on specific dates.
More information is available on this website .
Festival Of Thrills isn't just limited to Halloween activities. Head to Weave for all things motorsport, with racing games, a full-scale race car display and bar games.
More information is available on this website .
Other activities that are part of Festival Of Thrills include a treasure hunt and a murder mystery game at Adventure Cove Waterpark and dining deals.

In a statement, Lena Lee, executive vice president of attractions and destination experience at RWS, said: “We are thrilled to set the stage and rev up energetic fun for this year’s Festival of Thrills with a dynamic line-up of Halloween experiences across RWS.

“Introducing more firepower to our eclectic range of offerings and event spaces across the property, we are reimagining the Halloween season in Singapore in an unprecedented, bigger and bolder fashion. We welcome guests to come explore and test their fear thresholds in experiences tailored to every fright level at our attractions, or just to soak in the races and Halloween-vibes season.”
Festival Of Thrills will run at Resorts World Sentosa till Nov 1. More information is available on this website .

listening.title: Singapore's Green Transit Push
listening.transcript: As Singapore aims to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050, the Land Transport Authority is accelerating the transition to cleaner energy vehicles. Commuters will soon see more electric buses on the roads, alongside expanded cycling paths in residential towns. These efforts are pivotal in reducing the city-state's carbon footprint and fostering a highly sustainable urban environment.

economistArticle.title: Surging bond yields presage pain—and not just for bond investors
paras: For over a decade, global investors grew accustomed to ultra-low interest rates, a placid era where capital was cheap and government debt seemed virtually costless. Today, that illusion is shattering. Government bond yields are surging to heights not seen in more than fifteen years, driven by a stubborn inflationary undertow and the fiscal profligacy of governments running massive deficits.

This relentless ascent in yields is sending shockwaves far beyond the narrow confines of bond markets. Because government bonds serve as the foundational benchmark for global finance, their rising yields act as a gravitational pull, dragging up the cost of borrowing for everyone else. Homeowners face exorbitant mortgage rates, while corporations find that the era of painless refinancing has abruptly ended.

The root of this seismic shift lies in a structural mismatch between the supply of government debt and investor appetite. Facing ballooning costs from aging demographics, green energy transitions, and geopolitical tensions, nations are issuing torrents of sovereign bonds. Yet, central banks, once the buyers of last resort, are now actively shrinking their balance sheets through quantitative tightening, leaving a deluge of paper to be absorbed by private markets.

The corporate sector is particularly vulnerable to this new regime. Thousands of firms that loaded up on cheap, long-term debt during the pandemic are now approaching a refinancing cliff. As these legacy loans mature, corporations must roll them over at punitive rates, a prospect that will inevitably squeeze profit margins and curtail capital expenditure.

Ultimately, the rise in yields portends a deeper, structural transformation in the global economy. Central banks, constrained by persistent price pressures, cannot easily rush to the rescue. Investors must now prepare for a protracted era where capital has a real, heavy cost, and where the fiscal excesses of the past decade will finally be paid for through slower growth and tighter credit.
economistArticle.cn:
十多年来，全球投资者已经习惯了超低利率。那是一个平稳的时代，资本低廉，政府债务似乎几乎没有成本。如今，这一幻象正在破灭。在顽固通胀暗流的推动下，以及运行巨额赤字的政府财政大肆挥霍的驱使下，政府国债收益率正飙升至15年多未见的高位。

这种收益率持续不断的上升，正向远超出债券市场狭窄界限的领域发送冲击波。由于政府国债是全球金融的基石，其收益率的上升发挥着重力吸引的作用，推高了所有其他人的借贷成本。购房者面临着过高的抵押贷款利率，而企业则发现，无痛再融资的时代已经戛然而止。

这一剧烈转变的根源在于政府债务供给与投资者胃口之间的结构性失衡。面对人口老龄化、绿色能源转型和地缘政治紧张局势导致的开支激增，各国正在大量发行主权债券。然而，曾经作为最后买家的各国央行，如今正通过量化紧缩积极收缩资产负债表，导致大批债券需要由私募市场来消化。

企业部门在这一新常态下显得尤为脆弱。数以千计在疫情期间借入大量廉价长期债务的企业，如今正逼近再融资悬崖。随着这些历史遗留贷款到期，企业必须以惩罚性的利率进行展期，这一前景将不可避免地挤压利润空间并缩减资本支出。

最终，收益率的上升预示着全球经济更深层次的结构性变革。受制于持续的价格压力，各国央行无法轻易出手相救。投资者现在必须为资本具有真实、沉重成本的长期时代做好准备，过去十年的财政过度支出，最终将通过经济增长放缓和信贷收紧来偿还。

gems.s: This relentless ascent in yields is sending shockwaves far beyond the narrow confines of bond markets.
gems.why: Uses personification ('sending shockwaves') and spatial imagery ('narrow confines') to vividly describe the broad, systemic impact of a financial metric. 它使用拟人化（‘发送冲击波’）和空间意象（‘狭隘的界限’），生动地描述了一个金融指标所带来的广泛、系统性的影响。

gems.s: As these legacy loans mature, corporations must roll them over at punitive rates, a prospect that will inevitably squeeze profit margins and curtail capital expenditure.
gems.why: Demonstrates a cause-and-effect logical flow ('As... must..., a prospect that...') combined with strong economic verbs ('roll over', 'squeeze', 'curtail') to deliver an authoritative analytical tone. 展示了因果逻辑流程（‘随着……必须……，这一前景将……’），并结合了‘roll over’（展期）、‘squeeze’（挤压）、‘curtail’（削减）等强有力的经济词汇，传递出权威的分析语气。
